# BladeMaster and DexLab: Running Softbody Cutting Simulation

This chapter uses DexLab's CPU cutting method. It cuts the tofu-like soft block in half and makes three continuous cuts like a banana, checks the independent scores, and generates a replay. DexLab refers to BladeMaster's TLMPM and persistent cutting history. The material parameters are set as synthetic ones, and real ingredients have not been calibrated yet.

## 1. First, watch the project demo

- [ Cut tofu in half: surface video ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/blob/main/docs/evidence/cutting/tofu/surface.mp4) · [ particle video ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/blob/main/docs/evidence/cutting/tofu/particles.mp4) · [ experimental instructions ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/blob/main/docs/site/zh/cutting.md). After cutting and removing the blade, a diagnostic impulse is applied to examine the independent motion of the two materials.
- [ Three continuous cuts with a banana: surface video ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/blob/main/docs/evidence/cutting/banana/surface.mp4) · [ particle video ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/blob/main/docs/evidence/cutting/banana/particles.mp4) · [ experimental instructions ](https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab/blob/main/docs/site/zh/banana-cutting.md). After three cuts, an independent scorer is used to check whether four connected components are formed.
- [ BladeMaster project page ](https://jango6324.github.io/blademaster/) shows demonstrations of robot cutting, pushing, and cross-cutting based on the original paper; the implementation uses GPU, while DexLab is a standalone CPU solution.

## 2. Windows Realization: From Simulation to Video

This time, DexLab cutting code was run using the existing Python 3.11 environment on Windows 11 and AMD Ryzen 7 5800H, and the solution is computed on the CPU. The project fully installs Python 3.12. In this case, `PYTHONPATH` is used to directly load the cutting module, and the complete DexLab task dependencies were not installed. The tested versions are: NumPy 1.26.4, SciPy 1.11.4, Numba 0.64.0, Matplotlib 3.10.6, imageio 2.37.0, imageio-ffmpeg 0.6.0, VTK 9.6.0, and Pillow 10.4.0.

Below, an environment is created and run from the source code in PowerShell; Git and Conda are required, and space is reserved for downloading dependencies. `$Tutorial` refers to the directory of this repository's chapter, which should be modified according to the actual location. The output and rendering directories for each experiment must be new paths.

```powershell
conda create -n dexlab-cutting python=3.11 -y
conda activate dexlab-cutting
python -m pip install numpy==1.26.4 scipy==1.11.4 numba==0.64.0 matplotlib==3.10.6 imageio==2.37.0 imageio-ffmpeg==0.6.0 vtk==9.6.0 pillow==10.4.0
git clone https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab.git
cd Dexlab
git checkout c7d958fe8bc1a2eb51429c95ae02f729f9176ef5
$env:PYTHONPATH = Join-Path (Get-Location) "src"
$Tutorial = "C:\path\to\every-embodied\10-具身智能其他仿真工具及仿真前沿\13-BladeMaster与DexLab柔体切割"
$Out = Join-Path $HOME "dexlab-cutting-output"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $Out | Out-Null
python -c "import numpy, scipy, numba, imageio, imageio_ffmpeg, vtk; print(vtk.vtkVersion.GetVTKVersion(), hasattr(vtk, 'vtkWin32OpenGLRenderWindow'))"
```

The last line should display the VTK version and `True`. Perform the two simulations in sequence; the program outputs progress based on simulation time, and a score is given at the end. Then run the scorer separately for another check:

```powershell
$Tofu = Join-Path $Out "tofu-run-01"
$Banana = Join-Path $Out "banana-run-01"
python -m dexlab.tofu_cut --output $Tofu
python -m dexlab.cutting_score $Tofu
python -m dexlab.tofu_cut --task banana --output $Banana
python -m dexlab.cutting_score $Banana
```

Confirm that the two ratings `passed` are `true`. The tofu is finally 2 portions, and the banana is finally 4 portions. `manifest.json`, `states.npz`, `trace.npz`, and `score.json` are saved in their respective output directories.

The official renderer uses EGL; Windows VTK provides `vtkWin32OpenGLRenderWindow`. In this chapter, [ windows_render.py](../../../10-具身智能其他仿真工具及仿真前沿/13-BladeMaster与DexLab柔体切割/windows_render.py) adapts the window class to a Windows off-screen window before starting the renderer, without changing the simulation state and score. Two records are rendered separately:

```powershell
python (Join-Path $Tutorial "windows_render.py") $Tofu --output (Join-Path $Out "tofu-media-01")
python (Join-Path $Tutorial "windows_render.py") $Banana --output (Join-Path $Out "banana-media-01") --stride 20 --fps 5
```

The banana is rendered at 5 fps with sampling every 20 frames to reduce rendering time, yet it still covers a full 8 seconds. Tofu uses the default sampling of every 5 frames at 20 fps. Each media directory contains `surface.mp4`, `particles.mp4`, corresponding GIFs, posters, and measurement files. Rendering is frame-by-frame, and the MP4 file is played after execution. If the output directory already exists, use a new one instead. This Windows process runs directly without using the resource limits and shared locks of systemd in Linux in the next section; on the shared machine, arrange the running window accordingly.

### Local Results and Replay

The independent evaluation for the machine-based tofu experiment is passed. There are two connected components, each accounting for 50% of the mass, with a relative displacement of approximately 3.221 mm; the cutting-induced motion includes diagnostic impulse. The default `cut-push` experiment for bananas also passes the independent evaluation. After three cuts, the components are 2, 3, and 4 respectively. The blade movement inspection is passed, with a relative displacement of approximately 10.209 mm in the pushed section. ## 3. Linux / WSL Official Environment

The following command is intended for Linux or WSL, using Python 3.12, Git, and a network accessible to PyPI. The official bounded executor requires running systemd, cgroup limits, and non-interactive sudo; WSL must first enable systemd. Simulation uses CPU; installing `cutting-render` dependencies is also required for generating surface playback. Ensure sufficient disk space, as the initial installation includes dependencies such as PyTorch. All commands are executed in the root directory of the DexLab repository:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/huangkiki/Dexlab.git
cd Dexlab
git checkout c7d958fe8bc1a2eb51429c95ae02f729f9176ef5
python3.12 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[cutting,cutting-render]'
```

This submission fixes the source code corresponding to this chapter. If you need to use a later version, please also verify its official experimental instructions. After installation, run `python -c "import dexlab, numpy, scipy, numba, vtk; print('dependencies OK')"`, and if `dependencies OK` appears, it indicates that these dependencies can be imported. If `python3.12` cannot be found, install Python 3.12 and its venv support first. If rendering fails, check the installation output of `vtk`.

## 4. Linux: Running Tofu Half Cut

DexLab provides bounded executors and shared research locks. First, specify the local output directory, the block device where this directory is located, and the shared lock path; `/dev/sda` is just an example. The actual devices should be identified through `findmnt -T "$CUT_ROOT"` and `lsblk`. All processes sharing the same research resources should use the same lock path; each `RUN`, resource plan, and receipt should use a new path. First, ensure that `systemctl is-system-running` can connect to systemd, and `sudo -n true` succeeds. The following uses a 4-core, 600-second setting as on the project experiment page:

```bash
CUT_ROOT="$HOME/dexlab-cutting"
mkdir -p "$CUT_ROOT"
findmnt -T "$CUT_ROOT"
lsblk
IO_DEVICE=/dev/sda                    # 改为实际块设备
LOCK="$CUT_ROOT/research.lock"
RUN="$CUT_ROOT/tofu-full-01"          # 每次换一个新路径
python scripts/bounded_run.py --profile adaptive \
  --resource-plan "$CUT_ROOT/tofu-plan.json" --cpu-cores 4 --io-device "$IO_DEVICE" \
  --data-dir "$CUT_ROOT" --timeout 600 --receipt "$CUT_ROOT/tofu-resources.json" -- \
  python scripts/research_guard.py run --lock "$LOCK" \
  --kind qualification --receipt "$CUT_ROOT/tofu-window.json" -- \
  .venv/bin/python -m dexlab.tofu_cut --output "$RUN"
python -m dexlab.cutting_score "$RUN"
```

The tofu baseline in the project record includes a 3-second simulation process: cutting, removing the cut, and applying a diagnostic impulse to one side. After the run, check `$RUN/manifest.json`, `states.npz`, `trace.npz`, and `score.json`. Based on the exit status of the independent scorer and `score.json`: the complete cut should form two connected components, and meet the displacement, contact, and numerical checks defined in the project. A successful exit by the runner only indicates that the recording process is over. This machine directly runs the tofu solver and the independent scorer using the existing Windows Python environment, producing two components with passing scores; the following Linux bounded execution chain has not been verified on this machine yet.

## 5. Linux: Run Banana Continuous Three Cuts

Continue using the new output directory under the same environment and repository root directory. This task takes longer than tofu; the actual duration depends on the machine and task version.

```bash
RUN="$CUT_ROOT/banana-full-01"
python scripts/bounded_run.py --profile adaptive \
  --resource-plan "$CUT_ROOT/banana-plan.json" --cpu-cores 4 --io-device "$IO_DEVICE" \
  --data-dir "$CUT_ROOT" --timeout 600 --receipt "$CUT_ROOT/banana-resources.json" -- \
  python scripts/research_guard.py run --lock "$LOCK" \
  --kind qualification --receipt "$CUT_ROOT/banana-window.json" -- \
  .venv/bin/python -m dexlab.tofu_cut --task banana --output "$RUN"
python -m dexlab.cutting_score "$RUN"
```

In the fixed version, `--task banana` defaults to `cut-push`: after making three cuts, continue moving the blade, with a full simulation duration of 8 seconds. If you want the diagnostic impulse version corresponding to the previous banana experiment, you can additionally specify `--motion-protocol impulse`, which takes 7 seconds. Check the cutting component and task results in the inspection score. The project also provides controls such as `--mode uncut` and `--mode partial` to verify whether the score rejects the complete four-segment task when not cut or with a shallow third cut. Each control should use a new output directory.

## 6. Linux: Generate and view playback

Taking the just-completed banana record as an example, the simulation reads the existing physical state without running a new simulation. The official recommendation is to perform it in a separate restricted post-processing window. The current source code uses `vtkEGLRenderWindow`, requiring VTK with EGL support and a functional EGL graphics environment. You can first run `python -c "import vtk; print(hasattr(vtk, 'vtkEGLRenderWindow'))"` for verification; if `False` is output, you need to install a VTK environment that supports EGL before rendering. Windows users should use the window adaptation described in Section 2. After rendering, search for videos and images in the output directory, and compare them with the official particle video in Section 1:

```bash
MEDIA="$CUT_ROOT/banana-media-01"
python scripts/bounded_run.py --profile adaptive \
  --resource-plan "$CUT_ROOT/render-plan.json" --cpu-cores 4 --io-device "$IO_DEVICE" \
  --data-dir "$CUT_ROOT" --timeout 600 --receipt "$CUT_ROOT/render-resources.json" -- \
  python scripts/research_guard.py run --lock "$LOCK" \
  --kind qualification --receipt "$CUT_ROOT/render-window.json" -- \
  .venv/bin/python -m dexlab.cutting_showcase "$RUN" --output "$MEDIA"
find "$MEDIA" -type f
```

Color indicates the cutting history; to determine whether the material is truly separated, one must consider the connection and cutting motion reconstructed by the scorer. In the time-step sensitivity results of the tofu experiment, the peak force values change significantly, and convergence in cutting force has not been established yet. It is suitable for learning numerical mechanisms, but should not be used directly as the cutting force of real ingredients.

## 7. How the cut is preserved

When the tool passes through the material, the solver records the cutting side for the particles; when particles and the grid transfer momentum, no incompatible coupling occurs on both sides of the cut surface. Thus, the cut remains intact after removing the tool, and material contact allows the cut surface to come into contact and slide again. The two-way interaction between the tool and the material causes the material reaction force to influence the movement of the tool.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[刀具运动和材料粒子] --> B[记录切割侧别]
    B --> C[按相容关系传递动量]
    C --> D[材料接触和刀具反力]
    D --> E[保存状态并独立评分]
```
